Hear How the FAA’s Ground Stop Unfolded

Air traffic nationwide came to an abrupt halt Friday. Radio broadcasts and messages between airline control rooms and pilots indicate how the industry navigated the crisis.

By

,

and

The Federal Aviation Administration’s move to halt all flight departures Friday afternoon shows the fragility of America’s air-traffic control infrastructure.

The extraordinary step, taken in response to disruptions in air-traffic control telecommunications, was the most severe nationwide ground stop since the terrorist attacks of Sept. 11, 2001. It threw airports into chaos, stranded tens of thousands of travelers, and snarled travel through the weekend.
